How does the external user management wo: How does the external user management work?
artwork does not check the password itse: artwork does not check the password itself for connected users – the identity check is done by the connected provider (OIDC or LDAP/Active Directory). The artwork account with all its roles, permissions and assignments is fully kept: the provider only replaces the password check, not the account.
The account is created automatically the: The account is created automatically the first time someone successfully signs in via the SSO button on the login page.
The account is created on the first logi: The account is created on the first login through the normal login form (e-mail + directory password) – or in advance via the synchronization.
The synchronization (\"Sync now\" or aut: The synchronization ("Sync now" or automatically every 30 minutes) imports all users matched by the user filter. Newly imported users receive a one-time welcome e-mail.
Newly created accounts automatically rec: Newly created accounts automatically receive the default role configured for the connection.
What happens with existing accounts (sam: What happens with existing accounts (same e-mail address)?
Every login and every synchronization ru: Every login and every synchronization runs through the same three steps:
The provider identity is already known (: The provider identity is already known (via its stable ID)? Then the linked artwork account is used and its profile (name, e-mail) is updated.
Otherwise: an artwork account with the s: Otherwise: an artwork account with the same e-mail address exists? Then it is linked to the provider and keeps all its roles, permissions and assignments. With OIDC this only happens if the provider reports the e-mail address as verified.
Otherwise a new account is created and r: Otherwise a new account is created and receives the default role of the connection.
The e-mail address is only used once – f: The e-mail address is only used once – for the very first link. Afterwards the account is recognized exclusively via the stable provider ID (OIDC "sub" or entryUUID/objectGUID). A changed e-mail address at the provider can therefore never take over a different artwork account.
If the e-mail address belongs to an acco: If the e-mail address belongs to an account that is already bound to a different provider, the login is rejected – an account can only be bound to one provider at a time.
Password login and password reset in art: Password login and password reset in artwork are disabled – the password lives at the provider. OIDC users sign in exclusively via the SSO button.
For LDAP the directory takes precedence:: For LDAP the directory takes precedence: if the e-mail address is found in an active directory, only the directory password counts – the local artwork password does not work as a fallback. Users that do not exist in any directory continue to log in with their artwork password as usual.
In the user overview, linked accounts ar: In the user overview, linked accounts are marked with an SSO badge; its tooltip shows the provider.
LDAP group mappings: roles and permissio: LDAP group mappings: roles and permissions configured in the group mappings are assigned and revoked automatically with every synchronization, based on the directory group membership.
Admin protection: the last admin who can: Admin protection: the last admin who can log in locally cannot be bound to a provider – this way at least one administrator with a classic password always remains.
Emergency access: the console command \": Emergency access: the console command "php artisan auth:break-glass" detaches an account from the provider and resets it to local password login.
OIDC: after saving a connection artwork: OIDC: after saving a connection artwork shows the redirect URI in the dialog – it has to be registered with the provider exactly as shown, otherwise the provider rejects the login.
